full_judgment:
5. Absconsion could not be a ground for presumption of guilt. 

 42. Convict Saiful Islam did never surrender and he was tried in absentia. Till today he is at large. Abscondence of an accused person in some circumstances may. not be an incriminating circumstance against him in respect of his guilt but long abscondence is an important circumstance against him and furnishes corroboration of the prosecution case. Sections 8 and illustration 'c' of section 9 of the Evidence Act are pressed in aid of the above proposition. In this connection, reliance may be made on cases, amongst others, Gul Hassan and another vs State, 1969 PLD SC 89, Muhammad Bashir alias Shikra vs State 1970 SCMR 351, State of Karnataka vs Lakshmanaiah (1992) 2 SCC 420. Therefore, the contention that absconsion could not be a ground for presumption of guilt does not hold water. "
